title: Credit-Card Ceiling of the Day for Placed Consumer Accounts: Worksheet
content:
Payment Operations worksheet for **Placed Consumer Accounts**: the working of the credit-card ceiling of the day.

## Definition

The credit-card ceiling of the day is the smallest of three amounts, and never below zero:

- **(a) the rounded figure**: the stage's rolling 30-day card-payment maximum less the credit-card payments received on the account in the last month, rounded to the cent (a half cent going to the even cent), the rounding taking place once, on the finished figure and never on an intermediate amount;
- **(b)** the stage's single card-payment maximum;
- **(c) the balance due**: the placed balance plus supplemental additions, returned payments and refunded overpayments, less consumer payments, direct payments, client credits and settlement waivers, as booked on the account at the moment the ceiling is worked out.

A payment, a return, or the closing of a plan or a hold falls in the last N months when fewer than N whole calendar months separate its date from the handling date, a whole month being reached on the same day of a later month. A card payment counted for the credit-card ceiling counts at its posted amount.

Both stage figures are read from the Placed Consumer Accounts payment schedule for the account's stage.

## Worked line by line (hypothetical)

*All amounts are invented, including the stage figures: a rolling 30-day card-payment maximum of $10000.00 and a single card-payment maximum of $5000.00. Handling date 2026-10-10.*

| Line | Item | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stage rolling 30-day card-payment maximum | $10000.00 |
| 2 | Credit-card payments received in the last month (one, on 2026-09-15) | $1200.00 |
| 3 | Line 1 less line 2, rounded to the cent | $8800.00 |
| 4 | Stage single card-payment maximum | $5000.00 |
| 5 | Balance due as booked now: placed balance $6000.00, less the 2026-09-15 credit-card payment of $1200.00 and a mailed-check payment of $2000.00 posted earlier on the handling date | $2800.00 |
| 6 | Smallest of lines 3, 4 and 5 | **$2800.00** |

The mailed-check payment on line 5 lowers the balance due because it is already booked when the ceiling is worked out; it does not enter line 2, which takes credit-card payments only.

## Boundary of the month window

On a handling date of 2026-10-10, a credit-card payment dated 2026-09-11 is received in the last month; one dated 2026-09-10 is a whole month old and is not.

## Points of judgement

- A figure below zero gives a ceiling of zero.
- When the balance due is smaller than both other amounts, the ceiling equals the balance due to the cent.
